info.bio: Los inicios de la banda se remontan al comienzo del año 1984 en la ciudad Seattle siendo parte de la primera oleada de bandas Grunge de esta ciudad. La formación tenia a Mark Arm como guitarrista y vocalista , Steve Turner como guitarrista , Jeff Ament en el bajo y Alex Vincent en la bateria para luego y rapidamente incorporar a Stone Gossard en la guitarra en reemplazo de Mark debido a que este queria concentrarse del todo en ser el vocalista.

scenes.name: Grunge
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El grunge, revival del hard rock de los setenta y renacimiento musical de Seattle, fue uno de los grandes fenómenos de los noventa (casi solo en EE UU). Green River lo inauguran (Come On Down) y Pearl Jam, Soundgarden, Melvins y Mudhoney fijan sus cuatro puntos cardinales; Nirvana, con Nevermind, lo convierten en una tragaperras y en la banda sonora de la crisis nerviosa de una generación. Después, Alice In Chains (Dirt), Foo Fighters, Hammerbox, GodHeadSilo, Everclear, Stone Temple Pilots, Tool (el grupo más innovador de la segunda generación: Aenima, Lateralus), God Machine, Helmet, Quicksand, Urge Overkill, los Smashing Pumpkins (Siamese Dream, Mellon Collie), Scarce, Creed, Bush, Manic Street Preachers, Silverchair.

podcast.title: Coined "Pure Grunge"
podcast.body: Mark Arm, a member of Green River and a coworker of Bruce Pavitt at the Musak Corporation, is credited with writing a letter to a local entertainment weekly in the early 1980s, describing a fictional band as "Pure Grunge." This is considered the first recorded instance of anyone in the area referring to the new Seattle sound with the "G-word." "In the early 1980s, he wrote a letter to one of the local entertainment weeklies. And he described this band, a purely fictional band, as Pure Grunge."

podcast.title: Deep Six Compilation Appearance
podcast.body: Green River was featured on the "Deep Six" compilation, an important record for the Seattle scene. The band included guitarist Jeff Ament, who would later form Pearl Jam, and Mark Arm, who had a day job at MuZac Corporation. "Other groups to appear on the Deep Six compilation included a new band called Soundgarden, a band called Green River featuring guitarist Jeff Amit, who would later go on to a former group called Pearl Jam."

podcast.title: Demise and Formation of Mudhoney
podcast.body: Green River ceased to exist in 1987, and from its survivors, including Mark Arm and Steve Turner, the band Mudhoney was formed, continuing the trajectory of early grunge music. "When they died in 1987, some survivors, including Mark and Steve, formed Mudhoney."

podcast.title: Early Grunge Candidate Status
podcast.body: Green River formed in the late 1980s, around 1988, and its members later joined Pearl Jam. The band is considered a strong candidate for being one of the first to make the leap into grunge music, pre-dating Nirvana's first album and being contemporaneous with Soundgarden's early activity. "nacen a finales de los 80 también, el 88, algunos miembros se perlían, habían sido miembros de Green River."

podcast.title: Early Grunge Pioneers
podcast.body: Green River was among the bands contributing to the early years of grunge in the mid-1980s, helping to establish the foundational sound. "It featured bands like the Melvin's, Mel function and Green River."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Formation from Mr. Epp and the Calculations
podcast.body: Formed by Mark Arm and Steve Turner "within weeks" after their previous band, Mr. Epp and the Calculations, broke up in February 1984, Green River quickly established itself as another "sludgy band" in the nascent Seattle scene. "Within weeks, Mark and his buddy Steve Turner formed Green River, another sludgy band who released a few records."

podcast.title: Grunge Pioneers
podcast.body: Formed around the same time as Soundgarden but recording first, Green River pioneered the grunge sound by building a template of "metal sludge plus punk speed" that became intrinsically linked with the Pacific Northwest. "Gene River, another Seattle band formed around the same time, but who started recording first, built a template of metal sludge plus punk speed that became associated with the Pacific Northwest Sound."

podcast.title: Members' Future Success
podcast.body: Guitarist Jeff Ament, a member of Green River, later went on to form Pearl Jam, a highly successful grunge band. Another member, Mark Arm, worked at the Musak Corporation warehouse and is credited with coining the term "Pure Grunge" in a letter, marking the first known use of the "G-word" for the Seattle sound. "Another group called Green River featuring guitarist Jeff Ament, who would later go onto form a group called Pearl Jam. Another member of Green River was Mark Arm."

xref.title: Formation and Major Label Debut
xref.body: Pearl Jam was formed as a result of the fallout from the band Mother Love Bone, and they proceeded to sign directly with a major label. Jeff Ament, a member of Green River, was a part of this formation. "And then there was the Fallout from Mother Love Bone, which eventually resulted in the formation of Pearl Jam, who also went right to a major."
